podcast.title: Conventional Release of In Rainbows (2007)
podcast.body: XL Recordings handled the conventional release of Radiohead's album "In Rainbows" after its initial pay-what-you-want digital experiment. This release contributed to the album's total sales exceeding 3 million copies. "More people bought the album when it was released conventionally through Excel recordings."

podcast.title: Vampire Weekend Album Release (2010)
podcast.body: The indie label XL released Vampire Weekend's "Contra" album in 2010, which included one of the band's biggest singles. "One of the biggest singles from Vampire Weekends Contra album, which was released on the indie label XL, was a song about a non-alcoholic Mexican drink that you might find at a hipster spot."

podcast.title: Adele's Indie Label
podcast.body: XL Recordings is the home label for Adele, and is considered an indie artist, making her the only indie artist to have sold more records than The Offspring's *Smash*. "Yes, Adele is an indie artist. Her home label is XL, part of the Bigger's Bank of the Group, part of the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Home to Adele
podcast.body: XL Recordings is the label for globally successful artist Adele, making her a certifiable indie artist due to XL's affiliation with the Beggars Group. "She records for XL, so she's an indie artist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Independent Haven for Radiohead
podcast.body: Following their departure from EMI, Radiohead signed with XL Recordings, an independent and relatively small record label. This move was significant because XL provided the band with complete creative freedom, allowing them to pursue their artistic vision without corporate constraints. "fichando con el quiz el recordings que es una disco gráfica muy independiente muy pequeña que les dejo hacer lo que quieren en la que a un movimiento continúa."
